brief.headline: Push for ₹1.87/bottle on PET amber 100 mL (16.6% cut) or walk to Suraj Blow Plast — and flip 30-day terms to 15-day faster payment against a 5% cut (they borrow at 10.27%)

priceAsk.summary: Cut the PET BOT AMBER 100ML/25MM NECK 12.5G from ₹2.18/NOS to ₹1.87/NOS
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹1.87/NOS to Suraj Blow Plast for the same bottle. TPAC's ₹2.18 is 16.6% higher. Match Suraj or we move the volume.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (cut from 30 days after receipt to 15 days) in exchange for a 5% price cut across all items
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster ties up ₹46539 of our cash, but a 5% cut is worth roughly ₹56600 a year — net win for us of about ₹10000, and it's worth 10.27% to them because that's what they pay to borrow money

brief.financialLeverage: TPAC is healthy — [ICRA] A / Stable rating, ₹637.48 Cr revenue, they keep about ₹4 of every ₹100 they sell (3.8% margin), debt is low (0.19x), and they threw off ₹35.20 Cr free cash last year. But they collect from customers in 67 days and pay suppliers in only 17 days, so their cash is stuck for 79 days — same as similar firms (79d peer) but still tight day-to-day. We're tiny to them (₹11.32 L is 0.02% of their sales), so we have almost no pull on our own. The play is to dangle faster payment (worth 10.27% to them) for a price cut, and to line up Suraj and the big converters so TPAC knows one 'no' and the volume walks.

evidence.point: We pay Suraj Blow Plast ₹1.87/NOS for the same PET amber 100 mL bottle; TPAC charges ₹2.18
TPAC borrows money at about 10.27%, so paying them 15 days early is worth that rate to them — roughly 5% annualised on the invoice
Their cash is stuck for 79 days (they wait 67 days to collect, pay suppliers in 17 days) — peer median is also 79 days, so cash is no looser or tighter than rivals
We're 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue — on our own we're invisible
They have GST filing delays and EPF payment delays on record — not a red flag for solvency (rating is still A / Stable) but shows admin strain
evidence.figure: GST filing delays, EPF payment delays

evidence.point: Market ask for a 28 mm PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typical ₹0.85–0.95); verdict is MARKET-FAIR with modest room to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter (₹2569.83 Cr, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms. Top second-source candidate, already qualified for our packaging.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr, health B 73/100) — pails, containers, pharma; strong and profitable, robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Suraj Blow Plast PVt. Ltd.
alternates.why: Already supplies us the same PET amber 100 mL bottle at ₹1.87/NOS — proven quality and price benchmark.

risks: We're 0.02% of their business — they can say no and not feel it. Bundle more SKUs or commit 2–3 years to get attention.
GST and EPF delays show admin stress; watch that invoices and compliance docs stay clean if we grow the volume.
Their Altman Z-score is 2.77 (grey zone) — not distressed, but not bulletproof either. Line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek before you squeeze too hard.
Market backup leads (Reliance, IVL Dhunseri, Ganesha Ecosphere, etc.) are not yet qualified — verify and price them before calling them alternates in the room.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We pay Suraj ₹1.87 for this bottle and you're at ₹2.18 — I need you at ₹1.87 or I move the ₹11 lakh to Suraj and Manjushree, but I'll pay you 15 days faster if you can also cut 5% across the board.
